faces.f:
"Peace hath her victories
No less renownd than war."
—John Milton,
"To the Lord General Cromwell"

"I will ... tell thee more than thou hast wit to ask."
—Christopher Marlowe, *Doctor Faustus*

"Cry havoc and let slip the dogs of war."
—William Shakespeare, *Julius Caesar*

"I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately."
—Henry David Thoreau, *Walden*

"And in their blind and unattaining state their miserable lives have sunk so low that they must envy every other fate."
—Dante, *Inferno*, trans. Ciardi

"Fire is the test of gold; adversity, of strong men."
—Seneca, "On Providence," trans. Basore

"The chill, to him who breathed it, drew / Down with his blood, till all his heart was cold."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, *Idyls of the King*

"Everything in Nature contains all the powers of Nature."
—Ralph Waldo Emerson,
"Compensation"

"One pain is lessened by another's anguish."
—William Shakespeare, *Romeo and Juliet*

"As if his chest had been a mortar, he burst his hot heart's shell upon it."
—Herman Melville, *Moby Dick*

"When good men die their goodness does not perish, / But lives though they are gone."
—Euripides,
*Termenidae*, trans. Morgan

"I am reminded of the fable of the silver egg. Its owner cracks it open to see what jewels it holds, only to discover a simple yellow yolk."
—Karn, silver golem
The air was filled with the cracks and snaps of flesh hardening as the new sliver joined the battle.
Bred as living shields, these slivers have proven unruly—they know they cannot be caught.
Titania rewards all who honor the forest by making them a living part of it.
One mogg to aim the catapult, one mogg to steer the rock.
It possesses no intelligence, only counter-intelligence.

"I can't hear them scream, but at least I don't have to listen to them beg."
—Phage the Untouchable
His bolas whirl like galaxies, but it's his enemies who see stars.
"If it didn't hurt, how would I know it worked?"
Once it consecrated the dead. Now it desecrates them.
Otaria's last defense against the wave of chaos threatening to engulf it.
It turns prey into predator.
Options will cost you, but a lack of them will cost you even more.
Stinking of rot, it leaps between gravestones in search of its next meal.

"I have seen and heard much here. There are secrets within secrets. Let me show you."
—Takara, to Eladamri

"You will learn to earn death."
—Volrath
"My family protects all families."

"I see more than others do because I know where to look."
—Saprazzan vizier
Hatred outlives the hateful.

"I am the purifier, the light that clears all shadows."
—Seal inscription

"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim."
—Sisay
We had taken refuge in a small cave, thinking the entrance was too narrow for it to follow. To our horror, its gigantic head smashed into the mountainside, ripping itself a new entrance.
It puts the "fur" in "fury."

"We decide who is worthy of our works."
—Gix, Yawgmoth praetor

"It was probably a lousy spell in the first place."
—Ertai, wizard adept
In fire there is the spark of chaos and destruction, the seed of life. In ice there is perfect tranquility, perfect order, and the silence of death.

"They are aberrations who have turned on everything we hold sacred. Let them be cast out."
—Ailheen, Speaker of the Council

"Don't laugh. It works."
—Yavimaya ranger
Like his mother before him, Darigaaz gave his life defending Dominaria from the tyranny of self-styled "gods."
They poured from the Skirk Ridge like lava, burning and devouring everything in their path.
It teaches *you* to play dead.
The pits have their own form of mercy.

"The hum of the universe is never off-key."
—Mystic elder
It's hard to be humble when the whole world is bite size.
Reach out and torch someone.
"The specimen seems to be broken."
A heart of light and a soul of darkness cannot coexist.

"The awestruck birds gazed at Wonder. Slowly, timidly, they rose into the air."
—*Scroll of Beginnings*

"The admixture of bitterwort in the viral brew has produced most favorable results."
—Phyrexian progress notes
Deep within the Cabal's vault, the Mirari pulsed like a dead sun-and its darkness radiated across Otaria.
Dominaria's most extravagant crypt nevertheless holds an empty grave.
Gaea needs no book to record every act.
The limbs of Pendelhaven extend as far as the meek roam, and reach as high as they strive.

"Think of this new life not as a gift from the angels but as a command to fight for their cause once more."
—War blessing of Serra
Root systems in Mwonvuli twist through currents of mana rather than soil.
Raissa transformed herself into a vessel for the Watchword Codex, allowing the arcane lore to flow through her body.
To the Krark Clan, every artifact has a trigger and a barrel.
Most myr monitor other species. Some myr monitor other myr.
Steady and silent as the deep current, the reejerey guides the course of the school.
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
Only in Ravnica do the wolves watch the flock.

"Even the threat of power has power."
—Jeska, warrior adept
Slain orochi warriors were buried with a tree sapling so they would become a part of the forest after death.

"May the memory of our fallen heroes ensnare the violent hearts of lesser men."
—Great Threshold of Monserkat inscription
Leylines branch out from its foundation like roots from a tree. These draw mana from every region and welcome all living things into its verdant chambers.

"He watches from above. He watches from below. He watches from within."
—Inscription on Tel-Jilad, the Tree of Tales
Before any major undertaking, a Cylian elf seeks the guidance of a visionary to learn the will of the gargantuan ancients.

"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid
An elder in one pride, of the Sigiled caste in another.
"You may enter the city—once the toll is paid."
"The Cloud Nacatl sit and think, a bunch of soft paws. We are the Claws of Marisi, stalking, pouncing, drawing blood."

"I search for a vision of Zendikar that does not include the Eldrazi."
—Expedition journal entry

Rhox monks are dedicated to spiritual growth and learning, and most bear the sigils of many students. However, they do not gladly suffer fools or those who disagree with their carefully wrought dogma.
"Brute force can sometimes kick down a locked door, but knowledge is a skeleton key."
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
Having flesh is increasingly a liability on Mirrodin.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
"Beg me for life, and I will fill you with the glory of Phyrexian perfection."

"Truth is always a weapon in your enemies' hands."
—Geth, Lord of the Vault

"We move because the earth does."
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad

"You serve Phyrexia. Your pieces would better serve Phyrexia elsewhere."
—Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane
If there's anything a werewolf hates, it's a collar—especially Avacyn's Collar, the symbol of her church.
"Avacyn's protection is everywhere. From the holy church to the sacred glade, all that we see is under her blessed watch."
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.
"May the worthy spend an eternity in Blessed Sleep. May the wicked find the peace of oblivion."

"My flesh holds no secrets, monster. The spirit of Mirrodin will fight on."
—Vy Covalt, Mirran resistance
Sometimes you die a glorious death with your sword held high. Sometimes you're just target practice.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."
Centaurs are sent to evangelize in Gruul territories where words of war speak louder than prayers of peace.

"It misses nothing and it has no sense of humor."
—Barvisa, courtroom scribe
Devil-blades and dripping blood make music Rakdos never tires of hearing.

"Dangerous to recognize. Deadly not to."
—Lazav

"The Simic come from the cold slow depths. How could they understand the fire in a wild heart?"
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.
"That must weigh heavily on your soul. Let me purge it for you."

"There is no time to remedy our enemies' ignorance. Blast it out of them."
—Aurelia

"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest."
—Nissa Revane
"Oathbreaker, I cast you out!"
Every world is a work in progress, constantly reshaped by time, disasters, and even the powerful magic of Planeswalkers.
"You thought only the gods could stop you?"
A stone hurled at an enemy is deadlier in liquid form.
Not an arrow loosed, javelin thrown, nor sword raised. None were needed.
The upside to not thinking about the consequences is that you'll always surprise those who do.
"You are beneath contempt. Your lineage will be forgotten."
Kolaghan goblins rush into battle to satisfy their desire for violence as well as their desire not to be eaten.
His beasts move the great siege towers of the Abzan across the endless sands.

"As the clans carved out their territories, we saw allies where the Mardu saw only obstacles."
—Yasova Dragonclaw
"He's paid his price. Now you pay mine."
The wave of lava seared cloth from skin, skin from flesh, and flesh from bone.
"You thought I wouldn't see that coming?"

"The mind of an Eldrazi is a puzzle that can never be solved. The trick is to make sure a piece goes missing."
—Jace Beleren

"All these old relics have one thing in common. Every last one of them is made of smithereens."
—Zada of Slab Haven

"We came to a place where the skin of Zendikar was peeled back and its bones lay bare to the sky."
—Greenweaver Mina
Inspiration comes in all shapes and sizes.

"As long as there is a single shred of life, there is hope."
—Nissa Revane

"For those without the Planeswalker spark, the merest touch of the Blind Eternities can kill."
—Ugin
Only one Eldrazi stood against them, yet the defenders were outnumbered.

"Dear brother, it's sweet that you have chosen to share your toys with Ludevic, but I too have found some new playmates."
—Ghoulcaller Gisa
"Let the flames ignore the sinless."
At Sorin's appeal, Olivia Voldaren summoned the full might of her bloodline to gather at Lurenbraum Fortress.

"More rope may not be necessary."
—Kep, Lunarch inquisitor
Uncertainty has its own allure.
"What's your plan?" Gideon asked. "Are you serious?" Chandra replied.
Impressing a judge is one thing. Delighting a child is another.
"I'd stand back if I were you."
It powers the dreams of Ghirapur.
The Hold, an illegal research facility in a derelict merchant ship, became a wellspring of renegade intelligence.
"This fight belongs to us all."
Once you have ascended to the highest temple of Orazca, the power of the Immortal Sun is yours to wield forever.

<< Tapez du poing,
Tapez du pied
Sur ma face de sagouin
Tant que vous voulez,
Demain matin, je serais sur pied. >>
- Moqueries trolls.

Les costumes d'accouplement des sylvins, surtour ceux de Ferracine, sont vraiment absurdes. Lents comme des tortues, on s'étonne que l'espèce survive à leur période prolongée de sélection, d'accouplement et de gestation.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
"This city is my home. I will make it a place to be proud of."
Some artisans spend their entire lives in pursuit of that one perfect creation.
Under the cold light of Innistrad's moon, with singsong rhymes and haunting whistles, Gisa delights in raising the dead to do her bidding.
A queen with no peer whose brood spans the sky.

"I have yet to discover a story that predates her. She may be as old as Ixalan itself."
—Huatli, warrior poet

"The emergence of the Eldrazi isn't necessarily a bad thing, as long as you've already lived a fulfilling and complete life without regrets."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter

"We pray to Avacyn on high.
On snow-white wings fearless you fly.
Keep safe our souls. Keep safe our lives.
May angels watch us from the skies."
—Children's prayer
"Better the dead depart utterly than be enslaved."
Her presence on the battlefield can transform an unruly mob into a disciplined army.
Some crime scenes' secrets can only be discerned from an angel's-eye view.
"Within every angel is a spirit of light that will fight as long as there is darkness."
In their final moments, the demons gazed upon grace in its purest form.
A righteous sovereign makes for a blessed realm.
The beauty of Valley is born from the differences between animalfolk, not despite them.
Clerics on both sides prayed for divine intervention to end the war. The gods didn't play favorites.
Her wings ripple with impossible colors—a sign that a miracle is on the way.
Gisela cornered the murderous demon among the graves of the dead villagers. "A fitting end," she murmured as she raised her sword.
Serra's grace most often manifests as a healing touch, but it may also grant a merciful death.
"I will not rest until you know peace."

"Strictly speaking, you can't kill what's already dead, but trapping and disintegrating it is pretty close."
—Garden, survivor technologist
Sensing a plot, Sorin raced to his grandfather's resting-crypt. But someone else had gotten there first.
Few escape the Underworld. Fewer still escape fate.
"I am the light that breaks the darkness."

"This city could certainly use a bit more divine intervention."
—Inspector Jillard
"Let's see how brave you really are behind all that oak and steel."
"You are not alone. You never were."
With their ancient enemy vanquished, the angels of New Capenna turned their eyes to their former captors: demons.
"You have not died until I consent."

"To halt these lurid practices, Geralf must be found and made an example of."
—Inquisitor Delmund
Strixhaven's five colleges encourage rivalries among the students, but some bonds transcend all barriers.
When Worzel summoned Segovian angels to fight Thomil's Gargantikari gnats, the ensuing battle numbered among the Multiverse's least destructive.
"Only when my sword lies idle shall I rejoice."

"Those who endure in the face of suffering, those whose faith shines long in evil days, they shall see salvation."
—*Song of All,* canto 904
"All are welcome in the angels' light."
"I do not fear death. I know my soul will rise to Starnheim, where I will feast forever among valkyries and heroes. Can you say the same?"
There may exist powers even greater than Phyrexia.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."

"Fear not the angels' constant eyes,
E'er on watch from lightless skies;
Eternal vigil will we keep,
Protectors of the Blessed Sleep."
She guides expedition parties through the perilous floating ruins of Zendikar's ancient empires.
"Well, this clearly didn't come from anyone I know . . ."
Before she is admitted to the host of Starnheim, a young valkyrie must learn a thousand tales of her ancestors.
"You can come back once you've learned some manners—and figured out how to reconstitute your physical forms."
The greatest masters of the craft abandon tools altogether, shaping metal with hand and mind alone.
"Only a mind unfettered with the concerns of the flesh can see the world as it truly is."
"Wasted potential surrounds us. Lend me that bauble, and let me see what it can be made to be."
For the Guidelight Voyagers, there is no such thing as junk.
"As one, nature lifts its voice to tell you this: 'No.'"
"Impress me."

"The cost of your opposition will be extracted from your wits."
—Nekusar, the Mindrazer

"I do things in my own time."
—Etha, initiate of Rhet crop
The Futurists eagerly supplement their research with their rivals' closely guarded secrets.
The indigo dragon gladly traded a bit of its hoard for everlasting moonlight.

"We are opening a new chapter in the one true story of Phyrexia. Someone must record it for posterity."
—Tamiyo
Tezzeret grinned as he realized Mm'menon was right: he had much to learn.
Every camera had a backup, and every backup had a backup, and every backup's backup had a backup, too.
It roams the skies over the Quicksilver Sea, alert for any hint of aberrant thought.
Vedalken eyes don't see the beauty in things. They see only what those things can teach.

"The Knowledge Pool knows. Memnarch understands."
—Janus, speaker of the synod

"Conquering your first world is the hardest, after all. My power grew as I moved from world to world, taking anything that would make the next taking easier."
—Ob Nixilis
Sometimes death comes knocking. Sometimes it tears down the walls.
Mourning shifts seamlessly to celebration as she chooses her next suitor.
It has no respect for the deeds of martyrs, reducing their legacy to a mouthful of flesh.
Every grave cradles a recruit.
"There's a smoothness to my magic here that I don't find on any other plane."
He rose from the graf for every cobbler, tanner, and fool who'd been slaughtered in the parish—and they rose and shambled after him.
While crossing the mire, Lort the Sneaky found the perfect shortcut to the end of his life.
For the necromancer barons, killing and recruitment are one and the same.
With Thraben's army recalled to its city walls, outlying villages were left to fend for themselves.
Sometimes she considered how much easier it would have been to stay dead.
Grixis is a world where the only things found in abundance are death and decay. Corpses, whole or in part, are the standard currency among necromancers and demons.
Having flesh is increasingly a liability on Mirrodin.
Death in form and function.

"Her voice is damnation, unyielding and certain."
—Phage the Untouchable

"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create."
—Liliana Vess
He wanders the Moorlands hoping to one day chop off a head worthy of replacing his own.
"There are so many of them. It seems they've just been waiting for someone to serve."
The Curse of Wandering leaves only hatred.
"Do not weep at your defeat, my dear. In death, you will serve a greater purpose—mine."

"Those who seize power must have the means to hold it."
—Queen Marchesa
No one welcomes his visit, yet all must grant him tribute.
Caught between life and death, between land and sea, between thought and oblivion.
For a ghoul, every village is a buffet and every disaster is a reunion.
Liliana developed a fondness for the moment when roaring becomes squealing.

"You foolish knights pound your breastplates and vow to fight until your last breath. As if that's when it ends."
—Tormod, the Desecrator

"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?"
—Vraska
Plague and death wrapped in one convenient package.
It was a night like any other. It would soon become a night no one would ever forget.
A spark of resistance against a tide of corruption.
Little agonies pave the way to greater power.
"Surrender your soul to me."
Necromancers deal in commodities far more precious than gold and grain.

"Even swamps need sustenance. We will give it to them, and in turn, they will sustain us."
—Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours

"To see past the veil of death, cross it."
—*The Red Book of Mezdrithalik*
It has the strength of seven men. In fact, it used to be seven men.
Those who don't learn from their deaths are destined to repeat them.
Even the lost and undead need a protector.
Each spindrell is the lingering consciousness of a survivor consumed by cellarspawn—a ragged, drifting remnant pulsing with constant psychic agony.

"What do you mean a walking clock destroyed all our cannons?!"
—Captain Lannery Storm

"Molten earth has no anger of its own. Only by infusing it with your own rage can the magma seethe and take shape."
—Koth of the Hammer
The peace summit proved the grudge between Urza and Mishra could end only in blood.

"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar

"My brother Thaedus's calculations were flawed. While correcting his work, I found that a dragon's fire breath can actually cover an area of—"
—Charred journal of Sophia the Cleverer
Sages whisper that Lathliss still keeps the heart of the old dragon queen sealed within a jewel, its smoldering warmth an eternal reminder that no monarch is untouchable.

"Look, I don't know what happened. And I really wish I did, so I could do it again!"
—Tailpipe, Rocketeer
In the moment before her execution, she realized what it meant to be a pyromancer, to be alive, to be Chandra.
"With your help, Loot, we're going to make a hell of an entrance," said Chandra. In less than fifteen minutes, she came to regret those words.

"The dragon is a perfect marriage of power and the will to use it."
—Sarkhan Vol
Atarka serving-goblins coat themselves with grease imbued with noxious herbs, hoping to discourage their ravenous masters from adding them to the meal.
"This world will be ruled by its rightful sovereigns, not these hideous pretenders."
"We speak the dragons' language of flame and rage. They speak our language of fury and honor. Together we shall weave a tale of destruction without equal."

"Spread out, you idiots! Spread out!"
—Marsden, party leader, last words

faces.f: In subsequent terms, first-year students were prohibited from enrolling in Introduction to Dragonkeeping.
The sparkmage shrieked, calling on the rage of the storms of his youth. To his surprise, the sky responded with a fierce energy he'd never thought to see again.

"Where will you run when I punish you with the very ground you flee on?"
—Nicol Bolas
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.
"Glory to the Burning Ones! May their mighty fangs devour all foes!"

"Surely it won't notice if I take—"
—Theria the Sly, last words
There were many reasons why Shiv was not high on Sheoldred's list of places to conquer: big, fiery reasons.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
The forge of Purphoros burns in the heart of Mount Velus, attracting dragons with its blistering heat.

"Remember all the great heroes who were careful and never did anything risky? Me neither."
—Syr Carah, the Bold
Attracting a dragon's attention may be the last mistake you make.
Nothing escapes its gaze—or its breath.
The fear of dragons is as old and as powerful as the fear of death itself.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"
Every movement is a summons—even your screams.
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.
"The tiniest mouse speaks louder to me than all the festival crowds on Tin Street."

"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them."
―Euphemia, Nexus watcher
Long ago, birds of paradise littered the skies. Thanks to the city's sprawl, most now exist as pets of society's elite.

"All the fancy spells and diabolical machines in the Multiverse are nothing compared to a good chomp."
—Vivien Reid
Sun Empire commanders are well versed in advanced martial strategy. Still, the correct maneuver is usually to deploy the giant, implacable death lizard.
For most, war is a calamity. For some, an opportunity. And for the very few, a pleasure.

"Might doesn't just build empires. It protects them."
—Inti, Sun Empire knight
After long days of squeezing through cramped tunnels, the Sun Empire's dinosaurs were overjoyed to stretch their necks and survey the wonders of the Core.
All the trees of the forest are his army, and every leaf his shield.

"I want to help Zendikar. Show me the way."
—Nissa Revane

"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest."
—Nissa Revane
"Slaughter the weak ones. They are unworthy of the gift of *compleation*."
"We could no more abandon the forest than the stars could abandon the night sky."

"He has learned much in his long years. And unlike selfish humans, he's willing to share."
—Garruk Wildspeaker

"Each tooth is the length of a horse, and new ones grow in every sixteen days. Let's get a closer look!"
—Vivien Reid
You don't want to know how she got that name.

"Life's greatest lessons don't come from focus or concentration. They come from breathing and simply noticing."
—Seton, centaur druid

"I watched him rip a Phyrexian dreadnought in half once. A few vampires will barely slow him down."
—Huatli
Those who die as heroes are permitted to dwell in Ilysia, a protected realm of the Underworld as tranquil and vibrant as the rest is bleak.
"This forest is your birthright. From now until your final breath, you and Llanowar are bound. Keep each other safe."
"Llanowar remembers the Ice Age, the Phyrexian Invasion, and the Rift Era. So long as we draw breath, we will ensure such disasters never threaten our world again."

"Regards from Peema."
—Rishkar

"I trust the instincts of any beast over the advice of any human who presumes to be an expert in the art of war."
—Rinshel, elf insurgent
"There are many kinds of duty, and mine is to see our world grow and endure."

"I don't know whether it hates the mycoids or just loves breaking things. I say we leave it be."
—Samin, Oltec scout

"Need a medic! And some stonemasons!"
—Wyllon, Drannith merchant

Initially frustrated by Muraganda's inconsistent biodiversity, Avishkari researchers made a breakthrough after mapping the plane's aetheric index—the wide variety of fauna was the result of raw magic, not evolution.
Raptors are clever enough to tear away a hard metal shell to get at the tasty morsel inside.
"Aether is the soul of Kaladesh, and all souls should be free."
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."
In nature, not a single bone or scrap of flesh goes to waste.
First, whispers of ancient days. Then, visions of things to come.
One eye open to see the truth of the world. One eye covered to gaze at the goddess within.
Two titans of Tarkir carved a swath through Phyrexia's elite.
"The greatest honor is to feed Atarka."
To keep the Reality Chip out of Jin-Gitaxias's hands, the Wanderer entrusted it to Tamiyo.
The Fang Druids call it the World Tyrant, for it has consumed entire ecosystems that it keeps suspended in its core. To look upon it is to see the world as it was eons ago.
No pain, no fame.

"I suppose we'll just hope those ancient monoliths lost to our people for centuries weren't particularly important."
—Toxayac, Sun Empire historian
With the cycles of day and night unspooled, the twisted sway of the moon only grew. And grew.

"Ixalli's fertile rays enliven us all. Each of us is a testament to the sun's strength and love."
—Chitlati, Lightning Rider
Its greatest asset is neither its sticky tongues nor keen eyes, but patience.
She speaks only in whispers but can be heard over the fiercest storm.
"I can call an army to my side in the blink of an eye. Best not blink."

"Release that which was never caged."
—Spellbomb inscription
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
Some patriars pay massive sums for exotic pets that can give their posh, predictable lives an edge of danger.

"The worthy shall strive for greatness. Supremacy in life leads to supremacy in the afterlife."
—Monument inscription
The essence of night to harden the soul.
The foundries of Kaladesh run like clockwork under the supervision of their formidable overseers.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
One part unstoppable force, one part immovable object.
Jeskai scholars fashioned devices to forecast the behavior of the dragonstorms.
Guarded by cartographers, disdained by warlords, coveted by adventurers.
The essence of flame to stoke the spirit.

"We shall forever roam."
—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims
Automaton inspectors ensure that the Consulate's stringent standards for mass production are upheld.

"The worthy shall rush to the God-Pharaoh's side with relentless zeal, rising to overcome every obstacle."
—Monument inscription

"You've begun to understand the hedrons' true purpose," said Ugin. "The Eldrazi can be imprisoned."
"And how did that work out last time?" asked Jace.

"Our glorious infection has taken hold."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite

"The courier's death was regrettable, but then again, she was warned not to touch it."
—Lord Xander
The essence of sunlight to brighten the way.
The impact sent the soldiers scattering—then something came out of the crater.

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer
"Ideas drift like petals on the wind. I have only to lift my face to the breeze."
